reading.body:
NTT VA7 publishes 36 MW of IT capacity across 125,000 square feet of technical space in Ashburn, Virginia, placing it twelfth among the nineteen Virginia facilities that disclose power figures publicly.

Power density at VA7 is roughly 288 watts per square foot of technical space. This density sits between enterprise and hyperscale workload profiles. At 40 kW per rack, typical of AI training, 36 MW supports approximately 900 racks. At 10 kW per rack, common in legacy enterprise deployments, the same power supports around 3,600 racks. The operator has not published rack count, cooling architecture, or power usage effectiveness, so which density class this facility actually operates at remains unknown from the disclosed data.

Among Virginia's 326 mapped data center facilities, only 19 publish megawatt figures. The nineteen publishing sites declare 1,326 MW combined, meaning VA7's share is 2.7 percent. Ashburn hosts the densest concentration of data center capacity in Virginia and ranks among the densest markets globally. The remaining 307 facilities in the state have disclosed no capacity figures this source has retrieved, so the true distribution of power and the actual rank of VA7 within all Virginia facilities cannot be determined.
